newsitem.title: USA: Rising costs overshadow record year at box office.
newsitem.headline: Rising costs overshadow record year at box office.

text.p: Hollywood had its most successful year ever in 1996, with box office receipts rising 7.6 percent to a record $5.9 billion and the biggest annual gain in moviegoers in almost 40 years.

However, according to figures released late Tuesday by the Motion Picture Association of America, the cost of producing and marketing a film rose even faster, casting a shadow on an otherwise upbeat year.

During a presentation at the annual ShoWest convention in Las Vegas, MPAA President Jack Valenti said the average negative cost, an industry term for the costs of making the film, printing copies and advertising, rose 9.5 percent last year to a new high of $39.8 million.
The costs of marketing a film rose 11.9 percent to $19.8 million, pushing the average cost for production and marketing a film in 1996 to $59.7 million, up 10.4 percent.
Over the last 10 years, Valenti said average costs have soared 148 percent.
Rising costs have prompted a number of studios to revise their strategy.
Last week, Walt Disney Co. said it planned to reduce the number of films it releases each year and to focus on high-profile, star-driven films like "The Rock" and "Ransom".

The focus on costs detracted from an otherwise solid year at the box office. Valenti said more than 1.34 billion tickets were sold last year, up 6 percent. The yearly gain was the largest increase in almost 40 years.
In addition, the frequency of movie-going increased 15.7 percent last year with moviegoers going to thheaters 8.1 times in 1996 vs. 7 times in 1995.
